ios.desc:
ReceiptIQ AI reads every line item on a receipt, not just the total — so you see what you actually bought, not only what you spent. On iPhone, iPad and Mac, with one purchase.

PERFECT FOR

• Freelancers and landlords who need itemized receipts at tax time
• Families sharing one budget across up to four devices
• Anyone tracking expenses who wants the items, not just a number

Point the camera at a receipt and let go. It waits until the paper is flat and in focus, then takes the shot itself. Seconds later the shop, the date, the tax and each individual item are filed and categorised.

Long receipts work too: show the camera the top, then the bottom, and both parts are joined into one receipt, or join two photos from your library. Each receipt also keeps its payment method (card type and last 4 digits), time, receipt number, seller tax number and tax per rate. Edit them, search by them and find them in CSV and PDF exports.

WHAT IT CAPTURES

• Paper receipts, with the camera on iPhone or iPad.
• E-receipts and screenshots. Share an Amazon order, an Uber receipt or an emailed invoice into the app from the share sheet.
• Email receipts. Turn on your personal forwarding address and forward order confirmations to it; you review each one before it is saved. Your mailbox is never connected.
• On the Mac: photos, PDF files and receipts dragged onto the window.
• Bank and credit-card statements (Beta). Import the PDF from your bank, or a photo, and every row becomes its own transaction, with a review list before anything is saved. Card and account numbers are masked on your device.

WHAT MAKES IT DIFFERENT

• Every line item, not just the total. Search "latte" or "USB-C" and find every purchase that contained one.
• No double entries. Scan the same receipt twice and the app notices — same store, same day, same total.
• Tax on its own. Sales tax, recycling fees and deposits go into a Tax category, so they stop inflating your grocery spending.
• A camera that waits for you. Live edge detection and automatic capture — no tapping, no blurry retakes.
• Receipts in any currency. A receipt printed in yen, euros or Taiwan dollars is recognised and converted at that day's rate, with the printed amount kept alongside it.
• Tested on real paper. Every release is checked against hundreds of real receipts from Japan, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Canada and the US before it ships.

quotes.text:
Hi HN! I’m a solo iOS dev who kept losing track of where my grocery and shopping money was going, so I built ReceiptIQ Pro.

What it does:
- Scan any receipt with on-device AI/OCR and instantly categorize the items.
- Auto-build spending charts, budgets, and exportable CSVs—no manual typing.
- Works offline; iCloud backup/restore optional. No data leaves your phone unless you choose to.
- Small extras: warranty reminders, bill tracking, and income logging.

Tech bits:
- Swift/SwiftUI on iOS.
- Apple’s Vision framework + my own ML post-processing.
- A lightweight Python backend for optional analytics (not required for core features).

I’d love feedback on:
1. Onboarding—does it make sense without a tutorial?
2. OCR accuracy on longer/foreign-language receipts.
3. Budgeting UX—too much, too little?

App Store link https://apps.apple.com/ca/app/receiptiq-pro-ai-scanner/id6742335723

Thanks for reading, and happy to answer anything!
